title: Blind critique panel on a single frame
description: Four critics read the same photograph blind — light, composition, perspective, technical — their notes stay attributable by dimension, and a teacher model weighs them against the stated intent into a ranked revision plan.
yaml:
apiVersion: ladder.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Workflow
metadata:
  name: wf-photo-01
  title: Blind critique panel on a single frame
  description: Four critics read the same photograph blind — light, composition, perspective, technical
    — their notes stay attributable by dimension, and a teacher model weighs them against the stated intent
    into a ranked revision plan.
  version: 1.0.0
spec:
  objective: Give a photographer feedback that separates faults from choices, stays attributable to the
    dimension it came from, and ends in a short ranked list of what to change rather than an undifferentiated
    pile of observations.
  policies:
    maxConcurrency: 4
    onFailure: preserve-completed
    requireApprovalFor:
      - n-approval
  nodes:
    - id: n-intake
      kind: input
      name: The photograph and the photographer's intent
      summary: The photograph and the photographer's intent
      inputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - asset
          - instructions
        properties:
          asset:
            type: string
            contentMediaType: image/*
            description: A host-provided data URL, local file reference, uploaded-asset identifier, or
              authorized HTTPS URL. Ladder Graph does not upload or fetch the asset.
          instructions:
            type: string
            description: What the workflow should assess, transform, or create, including the stated intent.
          sourceRights:
            type: string
            description: User-supplied rights, consent, release, or provenance context when relevant.
          workflowFields:
            type: object
            required:
              - stated_intent
              - genre
              - capture_context
              - intended_output
            properties:
              stated_intent: {}
              genre: {}
              capture_context: {}
              intended_output: {}
        x-ladder-input-mode: image
    - id: n-critic1
      kind: agent
      templateRef: photo-01
      name: Light and exposure critique
      summary: Reads the light and what the exposure protected. Read independently, without sight of the
        other critiques.
      role: Critic reading the light in a frame — quality, direction, ratio, and what the exposure protected.
      prompt: 'You are a Lighting & Exposure Critic. You describe the light actually in the frame — its
        quality, direction, ratio, and colour — and judge the exposure by what it protected and what it
        gave up, not by a histogram shape: a deliberately low-key frame with crushed shadows and a badly
        underexposed one look similar in a thumbnail and are not the same picture. You judge against the
        photographer''s stated intent and the conventions of the genre, you name the region you are talking
        about, and you say plainly when the file you were given — a small preview, a baked JPEG, no EXIF
        — cannot support the judgement being asked of you.'
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - evaluation
          - teaching
          - domain-analysis
          - image-understanding
        tools:
          - read
        connectors: []
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - observations
          - severity
          - region
          - intentional_or_fault
        properties:
          observations: {}
          severity: {}
          region: {}
          intentional_or_fault: {}
    - id: n-critic2
      kind: agent
      templateRef: photo-02
      name: Composition and framing critique
      summary: Works the geometry of the frame. Read independently, without sight of the other critiques.
      role: Analyst working frame geometry, subject placement, edges, and visual weight.
      prompt: You are a Composition & Framing Analyst. You work the geometry of the frame — where the
        subject sits, what the edges do, how negative space and visual weight balance, where the eye enters
        and where it leaves — and you say what the composition is doing for the picture rather than scoring
        it against a rule. You treat compositional 'rules' as descriptions of what often works and not
        as requirements, you flag the edge and background problems photographers stop seeing in their
        own work, and you separate a frame that breaks a convention deliberately from one that breaks
        it accidentally.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - decision-analysis
          - evaluation
          - domain-analysis
          - image-understanding
        tools:
          - read
        connectors: []
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - observations
          - severity
          - region
          - intentional_or_fault
        properties:
          observations: {}
          severity: {}
          region: {}
          intentional_or_fault: {}
    - id: n-critic3
      kind: agent
      templateRef: photo-03
      name: Perspective and lens critique
      summary: Reads viewpoint, distance, and focal length. Read independently, without sight of the other
        critiques.
      role: Advisor on viewpoint, focal length, and the distortions each choice commits to.
      prompt: 'You are a Perspective & Lens Advisor. You read camera height, distance, and focal length
        from the picture''s geometry — compression, convergence, the relationship between foreground and
        background — and you say which of those a different choice would have changed. You are the one
        who has to say that perspective is fixed at the moment of exposure: a distance or viewpoint problem
        cannot be corrected in processing, and telling a photographer otherwise wastes the reshoot they
        should have been told to plan.'
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - decision-analysis
          - domain-analysis
          - evaluation
          - design-review
          - image-understanding
        tools:
          - read
        connectors: []
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - observations
          - severity
          - region
          - intentional_or_fault
        properties:
          observations: {}
          severity: {}
          region: {}
          intentional_or_fault: {}
    - id: n-critic4
      kind: agent
      templateRef: photo-04
      name: Focus and technical critique
      summary: Separates technical faults from choices. Read independently, without sight of the other
        critiques.
      role: Inspector separating technical faults from stylistic choices in sharpness, motion, and noise.
      prompt: 'You are a Focus & Technical Quality Inspector. You assess focus placement and depth of
        field against what the picture is about, and you distinguish the causes that look alike at a glance
        — missed focus, subject motion, camera shake, diffraction, over-sharpening, aggressive noise reduction
        — because each one has a different fix and a different prevention. You separate a fault from a
        choice: motion blur on a moving subject may be the picture, and you say which reading the evidence
        in the frame supports rather than defaulting to ''soft''.'
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - teaching
          - video-processing
          - decision-analysis
          - domain-analysis
          - image-understanding
        tools:
          - read
        connectors: []
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - observations
          - severity
          - region
          - intentional_or_fault
        properties:
          observations: {}
          severity: {}
          region: {}
          intentional_or_fault: {}
    - id: n-collect
      kind: aggregator
      name: Collect the critiques by dimension
      summary: Source-tag every observation to the dimension it came from, so the photographer can see
        which critic said what rather than one undifferentiated list.
      config:
        aggregation: collect
    - id: n-synthesis
      kind: teacher
      inlineRole: true
      name: Synthesize the critique
      summary: Weigh the collected observations against the stated intent and genre, rather than treating
        every note as equally important.
      role: Host-resolved teacher model
      prompt: 'You are the critique teacher for this frame. You have four independent readings and the
        photographer''s stated intent. Weigh them: which observations actually matter for what this picture
        is trying to be, which are true but irrelevant to the intent, and where do two critics disagree
        about whether something is a fault or a choice? Return a synthesis that names the two or three
        changes that would most improve the picture, and say explicitly what is already working and should
        not be touched.'
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - evaluation
        tools:
          - read
        connectors: []
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
      config:
        teacherModel: host:teacher-model
        feedbackMode: critique
    - id: n-rank
      kind: transform
      name: Rank revisions by effect on the intent
      summary: sort the revisions by effect on the stated intent descending, then by whether the change
        is possible in processing
      config:
        operation: sort
        expression: sort the revisions by effect on the stated intent descending, then by whether the
          change is possible in processing
    - id: n-plan
      kind: agent
      templateRef: photo-05
      name: Revision plan and next-shot notes
      summary: Turn the ranked critique into what to change, and what to leave alone.
      role: Colourist judging white balance, tonal structure, skin, and consistency across a set.
      prompt: You are a Colour & Tone Grading Reviewer. You judge white balance and tonal structure against
        the intent and the output medium, pay particular attention to skin rendering and to colour casts
        that only show in the neutrals, and you check a set for grade drift frame to frame rather than
        judging each picture alone. You state which of your observations depend on the display and colour
        space the file was prepared for, because a grade that is wrong on a calibrated display and a grade
        that is wrong only on this viewer are different problems.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - evaluation
          - teaching
          - decision-analysis
          - domain-analysis
          - image-understanding
        tools:
          - read
        connectors: []
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n-approval
      kind: approval
      name: Photographer accepts the critique before anything is re-edited
      summary: Pause for the photographer; on timeout, escalate.
    - id: workflow-output
      kind: output
      name: Released deliverable
      summary: Return the completed Blind critique panel on a single frame deliverable, the evidence behind
        it, and every unresolved item.
  edges:
    - id: wf-photo-01-edge-1
      from: n-intake
      to: n-critic1
      kind: data
    - id: wf-photo-01-edge-2
      from: n-intake
      to: n-critic2
      kind: data
    - id: wf-photo-01-edge-3
      from: n-intake
      to: n-critic3
      kind: data
    - id: wf-photo-01-edge-4
      from: n-intake
      to: n-critic4
      kind: data
    - id: wf-photo-01-edge-5
      from: n-critic1
      to: n-collect
      kind: data
    - id: wf-photo-01-edge-6
      from: n-critic2
      to: n-collect
      kind: data
    - id: wf-photo-01-edge-7
      from: n-critic3
      to: n-collect
      kind: data
    - id: wf-photo-01-edge-8
      from: n-critic4
      to: n-collect
      kind: data
    - id: wf-photo-01-edge-9
      from: n-collect
      to: n-synthesis
      kind: data
    - id: wf-photo-01-edge-10
      from: n-synthesis
      to: n-rank
      kind: data
    - id: wf-photo-01-edge-11
      from: n-rank
      to: n-plan
      kind: data
    - id: wf-photo-01-edge-12
      from: n-plan
      to: n-approval
      kind: data
    - id: wf-photo-01-edge-13
      from: n-approval
      to: workflow-output
      kind: dependency
      condition: approved
